finding.claim: The authenticated identity is taken directly from a client-supplied HTTP header, `X-Session-User-Verified`. Nothing in this code verifies a session, signature or proxy origin, so any client can impersonate any user, including a resource owner. The header name suggests a trusted front proxy sets it, but the app never checks that, and it does not strip or reject the header when it arrives from outside. If the app is reachable without a proxy that overwrites the header, authorization is bypassed. If such a proxy exists, the finding is not exploitable.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled request header X-Session-User-Verified, which the attacker can set to any username
finding.sink: ensure_allowed / is_allowed in the DELETE /files/<fid> and POST /files/<fid>/rename handlers, which guard `del STORE[fid]` and the write to f['name']

trace.note: ensure_allowed(g.user, f, 'delete') uses the spoofed identity
is_allowed looks up resource['grants'][user] with the attacker-chosen name, so naming a granted user passes the check
rename_file runs the same check with the spoofed identity

finding.guards_checked: before_request only copies the header. There is no signature, session or token validation, and no check that the request came from a trusted proxy. acl.py is_allowed is a plain membership check on the supplied username. ensure_allowed does abort(403) correctly in delete_file, and rename_file uses the result of is_allowed correctly, so the permission-result and async cases do not apply. A missing header gives g.user=None, which has no grants and is denied. Nothing else on the path stops spoofing.

verdict.guard_found: ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10) aborts 403 and rename_file tests is_allowed (views.py:25), but both check only the spoofable username; no session, signature or proxy validation exists in the repo (only acl.py and views.py).
verdict.reason: views.py:11 sets g.user straight from the client-controlled X-Session-User-Verified header, and acl.py:5 only checks membership of that name in grants, so a caller naming a granted user passes the checks at views.py:17 and views.py:25 and reaches the delete at views.py:18 and the rename at views.py:27; exploitability depends on a trusted proxy outside this code that strips or overwrites the header, which the repo cannot show.
